Chapter 7: Mastering Transitions—Making the Most of In-Between Moments
Have you ever noticed how much time slips away in those little gaps between activities? Maybe it's the commute to work, standing in line at the store, or that quiet lull right after a meeting ends. These are what we call in-between moments—and honestly, they can add up faster than you might think.
I like to think of transitions as the seams in a favorite piece of clothing. They're easy to ignore, but they’re absolutely essential for keeping everything together. If you start to pay attention to these moments, you’ll find you can actually reclaim time that would otherwise get lost to scrolling, daydreaming, or just feeling frustrated.
So, how do you make the most of these transitions? Here are a few practical ideas that really work:
First, try preparing for the next thing before you finish what you’re doing now. For example, if you want to work out after your workday ends, go ahead and set your shoes and water bottle by the door before you log off. That way, when it’s time to move, you’re already halfway there.
Next, use those short gaps for quick wins—what I call micro-tasks. Maybe it’s replying to a text you’ve been putting off, doing a quick stretch, or simply reflecting on how your day’s going. These little actions can make a surprising difference.
Don’t forget to build in some buffer zones, too. Leaving a bit of space between big commitments gives your mind a chance to reset. That means you’re less likely to feel overwhelmed and more likely to show up focused for what’s next.
Here’s a real-world example: imagine a parent who always feels frazzled after work. Instead of rushing straight home, they use the commute to listen to their favorite playlist or practice a few deep breaths. That small shift carves out a boundary between work and family time—and it can make all the difference in being present for the people who matter most.
One more thing—these in-between moments are perfect opportunities to practice gratitude or mindfulness. Just pausing to notice the transition from one part of your day to the next can bring a sense of closure and fresh intention, instead of feeling like you’re just being swept along by the rush.
So, next time you catch yourself in a transition, ask yourself—how could I use this moment to recharge, reset, or move just a little closer to my goals?
